fullPassage: In the workplace, it’s vital that communication go both ways. People must be able to ask questions and offer critiques and ideas. Ideally, they should be able to do so with all managers, up to the CEO. At new employee college, we’d say to the participants, “You will take out of this day what you put into it. If you don’t ask questions, you won’t get answers.” I look back now and realize that this was crucial early stage-setting for the success of the company. It gave people at all levels license to freely ask for clarification, whether about something they were expected to do or about a decision made by management. Not only did this mean they were better informed, but over time it instilled throughout the company a culture of curiosity. That meant managers often gained important insights because someone had asked a really good question.

questions.passage: In the workplace, it’s vital that communication go both ways. People must be able to ask questions and offer critiques and ideas. Ideally, they should be able to do so with all managers, up to the CEO. At new employee college, we’d say to the participants, “You will take out of this day what you put into it. If you don’t ask questions, you won’t get answers.” I look back now and realize that this was crucial early stage-setting for the success of the company. It gave people at all levels license to freely ask for clarification, whether about something they were expected to do or about a decision made by management. Not only did this mean they were better informed, but over time it instilled throughout the company a culture of curiosity. That meant managers often gained important insights because someone had asked a really good question.
questions.stem: 윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: ② 질문 없이도 정보를 얻을 수 있다는 진술은 본문(질문 안 하면 답을 못 얻음)과 모순된다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 'communication go both ways', 'up to the CEO'와 일치
❌ ② 본문은 "If you don't ask questions, you won't get answers(질문하지 않으면 답을 얻지 못한다)"라고 했으므로, '질문 없이도 정보를 얻을 수 있다'는 진술은 불일치 ←정답
✅ ③ 'Not only did this mean they were better informed'와 일치
✅ ④ 'managers often gained important insights because someone had asked a really good question'과 일치
det.tip: 불일치 문제는 본문이 부정하거나 반대로 말한 선지를 찾는다

ch: 소통은 CEO를 포함한 모든 관리자와 양방향으로 이루어질 수 있어야 한다.

좋은 질문 덕분에 관리자들이 중요한 통찰을 얻기도 했다.

det.korean: ③ to freely asking → to freely ask: 'license to + 동사원형' 구조이므로 (부사 freely를 사이에 두더라도) 동사원형 ask가 맞다.

det.tip: to + (부사) + 동사원형. license to (freely) ask (O) / asking (X)

다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로, 1단어)

expect → ____

det.korean: be동사(were) 뒤에서 '~하도록 기대되다'라는 수동의 의미를 나타내므로 과거분사 expected로 바꾼다.
det.analysis: 빈칸 앞에 be동사 were가 있어요. 'be동사 + 과거분사(p.p.)'는 '~되다(수동)'라는 뜻이에요. 'they were ___ to do(그들이 하도록 기대되는)'라는 수동 의미가 되어야 하므로 expect를 과거분사 expected로 바꿔야 해요. 'something they were expected to do(그들이 하도록 기대되는 일)'가 됩니다.
det.tip: be동사(were) + 과거분사(expected) + to do = ~하도록 기대되다. expect → expected

det.korean: someone had asked a really good question: 누군가가 정말 좋은 질문을 했었다.

someone(1) had(2) asked(3) a(4) really(5) good(6) question(7) = 7단어
det.tip: someone had asked + a(관사) really(부사) good(형용사) question(명사)
